reading.body:
Microsoft does not publish power capacity, square footage, or exact specifications for individual Azure data center campuses, including this Quincy facility. The operator discloses only aggregate worldwide statistics: 500+ datacenters across 80+ regions, 40+ gigawatts of renewable energy contracted globally, and 800,000+ kilometers of network fiber. This disclosure policy makes the campus's actual size and role in AI scaling invisible to external analysis.

The Quincy campus is one of Microsoft's oldest and most significant hyperscale facilities, established around 2007 and now part of a two-county Central Washington region spanning Quincy and East Wenatchee. Washington state has 46 mapped data center facilities, but only 2 publish power capacity figures; those two total 60 MW of disclosed capacity, placing this campus third by published MW in the state, though its actual power draw remains undisclosed.

Microsoft's own local community pages and regional press coverage, including a 2022 public tour event for a new Douglas County facility in the region, confirm the strategic scale of Central Washington as a data center transformation hub. Without published specifications for this individual campus, its contribution to AI training density, grid demand, or Microsoft's hyperscale buildout cannot be quantified from operator disclosures alone.
